conflicts.fact: Number of lessons in the unit / how many lessons remain
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says the class will spend 'the next 12 lessons' (13 total, consistent). Lesson 9 says 'Lessons 10 through 13' will address questions (consistent). Lesson 13 says 'twelve lessons' of evidence while its Observed says 'thirteen lessons' of knowledge; Lesson 10 says 'nine lessons' (fine).

conflicts.fact: Whether graphite and the diamond/graphite data are part of the tested set, and what the unknown samples are
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 predicts for four unknowns (NaCl, sugar, SiO2, aluminium) plus diamond and graphite as bonus unknowns E and F. Lesson 8 tests five substances, with graphite powder as a tested substance, and does not test diamond. Lesson 9 works with four substances (NaCl, sugar, SiO2, aluminium), with graphite possibly only a teacher demo ('if it was tested'), though its Observed says graphite conducted. The dataset changes between lessons.

conflicts.fact: Where graphite's delocalised electrons are located and the model used
conflicts.versions: Lessons 4, 9 and 12 say one delocalised electron per carbon, free to move within/across the layer (L6: 'within each layer'). Lessons 9 and 11 say 'between layers' / 'between layers' pi electrons. Lesson 6 says within each layer, giving partial metallic character.

conflicts.fact: Station and timing details / the conductivity tester used in the demos
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 uses a 6V battery-bulb tester; Lesson 6 uses a 9V battery with an LED bulb; Lesson 8 timing says three stations of about 18 minutes each plus transitions, while Lesson 11 says the class timing is a '40-minute' structure for Lessons 9 and 13 versus 80-minute for Lessons 3, 5, 8, 10.

conflicts.fact: When the graphite/diamond conductivity experiment was done and its relation to NaCl/diamond solubility
conflicts.versions: Lesson 11 says 'our bulb-and-wire experiment last week' and refers to the Lesson 8 solubility investigation comparing NaCl dissolving with diamond not dissolving, but Lesson 8 never tested diamond (only graphite, SiO2, etc.).

conflicts.fact: Who owns the cumulative model and its form
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 stores the initial model in an individual 'Model Envelope' and Lesson 3 a 'Bonding Model' booklet; Lesson 4 uses a class A2 poster; Lesson 8 says the Bond-Type Property Model has been building since Lesson 5 (not Lesson 1); Lesson 7 uses a group poster.

conflicts.fact: What SiO2 is used for / its properties
conflicts.versions: Lesson 10 says SiO2's giant covalent network gives transparency (glass-making) and Lesson 12 says SiO2 is tetrahedral; Lesson 7 describes sand as grey-white and Lesson 8 as river-bed sand; not a direct conflict but glass is not pure SiO2 sand. Lesson 9 describes only 'four' substances where Lesson 8 had five.
